doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Sexism: a San Diego club refuses a raise
summary: Jeannie recounts a club owner on Harbor Island who would not raise her pay unless the organist got one because he was a man.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Not only race but sexist. So I get a double whammy. We played for a guy, remember the guy right here in San Diego. And so we came to the place, and this organist was sitting there playing to the bartender. So we told him we wanted to start a jam session. He says, he’s from St. Louis, he says, “Oh, okay.” He says, “Peanuts Hucko is my friend.” He
says, “I know all about jam sessions.” We got this jam session going, and you couldn’t move in there.

And so, after three weeks, and I said, “Jimmy, it’s time to hit for a raise now,” you know. So we went to the guy, and said it’s time for us to get a raise. He said, “I’m not going to give you a raise,” he told me. I said, “Okay then we’ll go somewhere else. He said, “No, don’t do that.” He said, “But if I give you a raise, I have to give the organ player a raise, because he’s a man.” I said, “But he’s not playing anything. When we came here he was just playing to the bartender. What do you mean?” I said, “But you can do anything you want with your money, as long as you give us a raise.” He refused to give me a raise without giving that guy a raise. He said because he’s a man.
And my mom always told me, she said, “When they talk like that,” she said, “just imagine them in boxer shorts and keep moving.”
Then come up with a great sense of humor.
